headline: Bison Range and Ranch Reservation Guide
reservation: The preserve is free to visit and individual visits do not require advance reservations. Group and school tours must be scheduled at least two weeks ahead. Check current guided-tour availability rather than assuming a bookable seasonal bus tour.

days.title: Ranching and Limestone Roots
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Visitor Center

stops.name: Spring Hill Ranch
stops.detail: Tour the 19th-century limestone mansion and the massive stone barn.

stops.name: Lower Fox Creek Schoolhouse
stops.detail: A short walk to a historic one-room school overlooking the valley floor.

days.driving: Minimal; most sights are within walking distance of the ranch
days.note: Sturdy walking shoes are needed for the gravel paths between historic buildings.

days.title: The High Prairie
days.start: Suggested: 7:30 AM from the Southwind Trailhead

stops.name: Southwind Nature Trail
stops.detail: A loop providing an introduction to native grasses and geological limestone layers.

stops.name: Scenic Overlook Trail
stops.detail: Hike into the backcountry to spot the resident bison herd and vast horizons.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes to trailhead; walking-heavy day
days.note: Bison are unpredictable; maintain a minimum distance of 100 yards at all times.

days.title: Flint Hills Scenic Loop

stops.name: Flint Hills National Scenic Byway
stops.detail: Drive through pristine prairie segments with numerous photography pull-outs.

stops.name: Chase County State Lake
stops.detail: A nearby spot for a quiet picnic and birdwatching along the water.

days.driving: Allow 2 to 3 hours for the loop; conditions vary
days.note: Gravel roads can be slick when wet; check weather before leaving paved highways.

intel.title: Visitor Center Hub
intel.text: Ample parking is available at the Visitor Center, though it may fill during spring burn events. Secondary parking is available at the schoolhouse trailhead.

intel.title: Prairie Dead Zones
intel.text: Cell service is spotty in the backcountry draws and along the Scenic Overlook Trail. Download offline maps and notify rangers of long hiking plans.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Fuel up in Strong City or Emporia before entering the preserve. There are no gas stations or food services within the preserve boundaries.

intel.title: Optimal Viewing
intel.text: Plan hikes for early morning or late evening in summer to avoid the 90-degree heat. Mid-day sun offers no shade on the open ridges.

intel.title: Trail Limitations
intel.text: Heavy rains can make low-water crossings impassable on backcountry trails. Check the Visitor Center board for daily trail status updates.

plan.arrival: Fly into Manhattan Regional (MHK), rent a car, and drive 65 miles south to Strong City to check in.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is suitable for the preserve, but high-clearance vehicles are better for county gravel roads.
plan.goldenHour: The Scenic Overlook Trail provides an unobstructed view of the prairie turning gold at sunset.
